text: This is Bob.
Bob is a hiring manager at a Belgian tech company.
Bob wants to hire a Brazilian developer.
The wiki is from 2019.
The AI assistant finds three versions of the process.
A meeting note says the opposite.
And nobody knows who owns it.
Don't be like Bob.
Bob went crazy.
This time Bob asks Recall.
He gets the current single permit process for Flanders,
not the 2019 wiki.
Two previous hires with the emails behind them and the one person who owns the process.
Sara checks a client's old doctor's note rule against the new sick leave law.
And Tom learns the old Amazon budget is gone and orders through the new IT portal.
Under the hood is TOKG, a temporal ownership knowledge graph.
Companies now produce more text than anyone can read.
Search finds everything, but can't tell what's current,
what applies to you, or whose word counts.
Step one, ingest.
Emails, meeting notes, wiki pages, and documents become facts,
shaped by a domain schema.
Step two, resolve.
Every new fact is checked against the graph.
It confirms what's known,
supersedes an older version while keeping the history,
or if a non-owner changes a rule, goes to the owner for approval.
Every fact carries three things:
when it's valid, who owns it, and the exact quote it came from.
Step three, serve.
FastAPI powers the app, and an MCP server lets any AI agent query the graph and cite its sources.
It runs in memory for zero setup or on Neo4j.
Answers you can trust, and a person to ask when the documents run out.
Why now?
AI made text free to produce, but trust didn't scale with it.
Knowledge management is already a twenty-billion-dollar market and none of it was built for AI-generated volume.
We started where rules change most and mistakes cost most, HR and payroll.
One partner like SD Worx reaches over a hundred thousand client organizations.
So every domain schema we built is reused thousands of times.
We sell B2B SaaS priced on indexed knowledge and query volume with private-cloud deployments for regulated customers.
The promise is a fixed oversight budget.
People set it up once and answer the occasional escalation and the graph keeps itself current.
Next come live Slack and Teams listeners
and alerts the moment a meeting contradicts policy.
Recall. Find it. Understand it. Trust it.
